findings.message: `unknownFor` is one set of people built from every hour that `loadInputs` reads, and `getReport` loads 12 months of hours so it can draw the trend (`view.ts:38`). `utilisationOf(inputs, range)` treats `inputs.hoursUnknown` as if it belonged to the month asked for, but it covers the whole year. So one week with an unknown status in any of those 12 months marks the person `hoursIncomplete` in the current month's table (null %, out of the team figure) and in every trend month too. It also adds a row for someone who has no hours in the month at all (`figures.ts` filter `inputs.hoursUnknown.has(p.userId) || …`). Fix: key the unknown set by person and day, or by person and week (for example keep the unknown rows' days), and in `utilisationOf`/`personFigures` mark a person incomplete only when an unknown-status hour falls inside `range`. Add cases where the unknown week is outside the month and in another trend month.
findings.scenario: Kasun has a copied hour in 2026-W14 (April) whose week Time no longer holds. Every October hour he has sits in approved weeks. Maya opens /reports for October → Kasun's row shows 'Some hours' timesheet status unknown' with no %, he is left out of October's team figure, and every trend month from April to October drops him as well.

findings.message: The newest-wins guard (`where reports.week_status.as_of < excluded.as_of`) orders a week's events by `core.event.created_at`. That column defaults to `now()`, which is the start time of the emitting transaction, not its commit order. A transaction that started earlier but locked the week and committed later (for example a reopen that waited on the approve's row lock) gets the older timestamp. Its status is then refused, and Reports keeps the stale one. No test runs two real transactions on the same week. Fix: order by something that follows commit order for the week (a per-week sequence or revision from Time carried in the payload, or `clock_timestamp()` taken after the week's row lock). Add a two-session test where the transaction that starts first commits last.
findings.scenario: Session B (reopen_week by an Admin) begins its transaction at t0 and blocks on the week row. Session A (approve_week) begins at t1 > t0, approves and commits. B then sees 'approved' and reopens. The events get created_at approved = t1 and reopened = t0. Reports applies 'approved' and refuses 'draft' (t0 < t1), so the reopened week's hours keep counting in utilisation.

findings.message: `below` and the lowest-first sort both use the raw `utilisation`, which ignores leave, even when a leave-adjusted `adjustedUtilisation` was worked out for that row. So 'Who is below 80% this week?' lists people whose only shortfall is approved leave. Fix: filter and sort on `adjustedUtilisation ?? utilisation`, or state in the tool's contract and description that `below` ignores leave. Add a table-driven case: no leave, leave that takes someone above the threshold, and leave the viewer can't see.
findings.scenario: Ayesha has 3 days approved leave in W43 and logs 16 h (target 40, adjusted 16). get_week_utilisation({ week: '2026-W43', below: 80 }) → she is listed as 40% and sorted to the top, though `adjustedUtilisation` is 100.

findings.message: `weekStatuses` is a new exported contract function with no contract test in Time. It is exercised only indirectly through Reports' tests, and no test checks that a week the viewer can't see is left out of its result. Time's README contracts list also doesn't mention it (the Reports README does). Add a contract test covering an own week, a visible team week, a week outside scope and an unknown id, and list the function in `modules/time/README.md`.

When the event's `core.event` row can't be read, `asOf` falls back to `new Date()`, so a failed lookup becomes 'newest event' and can overwrite a status that really is newer. Fail instead (throw so the outbox retries) rather than invent a timestamp.
findings.scenario: The event row has been pruned or isn't visible when a redelivered 'submitted' event runs → `as_of` = now, and it overwrites a later 'approved' status.
